title: The Big Leap
author: Gay Hendricks
subtitle: Break the upper limit. Live in your Zone of Genius.

chapters.title: Preparing for Your Big Leap
items: Identify your Upper Limit Problem — the inner thermostat that caps how much success, love, and joy you let yourself feel.
Watch for self-sabotage right after things go well; that timing is the diagnostic tell.
Ask the governing question daily: “How much love and success can I allow myself to enjoy?”
Map yourself across the four zones: incompetence, competence, excellence, genius.
Treat the Zone of Excellence as the trap it is — comfortable, well-rewarded, and not where you belong.

chapters.title: Making the Leap
items: Name which false belief holds you back: feeling fundamentally flawed, fearing success means disloyalty or abandonment, believing more success is a bigger burden, or fearing you'll outshine others.
Treat each barrier as an old fear, not a present fact.
Trace the belief to its childhood origin, then separate it from your adult reality.
Extend how long you let a good feeling last — push past your usual cutoff on purpose.
Choose expansion consciously each time the old story resurfaces.

chapters.title: Getting Specific
chapters.tag: Spotting the ULP in daily life
items: Catch worry that points to no real, actionable threat — it's an Upper Limit habit, not useful foresight.
Receive compliments and positive energy fully instead of deflecting them.
Audit your integrity breaches: broken agreements and truths left unspoken.
Recognize blame and criticism as ways you dump good energy.
Notice manufactured arguments, illnesses, and accidents that follow your highs.
Speak the significant truths you've been withholding.

chapters.title: Building a New Home in Your Zone of Genius
items: Answer the four questions: what you most love to do, what doesn't feel like work, what gives the highest results-to-effort ratio, and what your unique ability is.
Pin down your unique ability — the specific thing only you do best.
Reallocate time away from excellence activities toward genius ones.
Keep “wondering” as an open-ended practice rather than forcing a fast answer.
Commit to genius as a way of being, not a weekend hobby.

chapters.title: Living in Your Zone of Genius

mantra.label: Ultimate Success Mantra
mantra.text: I expand in abundance, success, and love every day, as I inspire those around me to do the same.

items: Deploy the mantra the moment you catch yourself Upper-Limiting.
Frame your growth as inspiring others rather than abandoning or outshining them.
Use it as ongoing course-correction, not a one-time affirmation.

chapters.title: Living in Einstein Time
items: Own that you are where time comes from — stop casting yourself as time's victim.
Drop “I don't have enough time” from your language and your thinking.
Locate where you're avoiding responsibility whenever you feel time-pressured.
Stop persecuting yourself and others over time.
Do more of what you love to expand your felt experience of time.

chapters.title: Solving the Relationship Problem

mantra.label: Ultimate Relationship Mantra
mantra.text: I expand in love and creativity every day, as I inspire those around me to do the same.

items: End the blame game by taking 100% responsibility — not a 50/50 split.
Spot the Upper Limit Problem in relationships: sabotage that kicks in after closeness deepens.
Speak unarguable truths (“I feel…”) instead of accusations (“you always…”).
Make clear agreements and keep them.
